body.text: Overview and Empirical Foundations of Energy in Japan
Modern physical infrastructure relies on precision systems such as Energy in Japan to deliver scale safely. Here is how engineers balance thermodynamics, material limits, and lifecycle cost.
Japan is a major consumer of energy, ranking fifth in the world by primary energy use.

Fossil fuels accounted for 67% of Japan's primary energy in 2023. Japan imports most of its energy due to scarce domestic resources. As of 2022, the country imports 97% of its oil and is the largest liquefied natural gas (LNG) importer globally.

8% of primary energy supply. Japan has committed to reaching net zero emissions by 2050, setting a target to reduce GHG emissions by 60% from year 2013 levels by 2035 and by 73% by 2040. In addition, the 7th Strategic energy Plan has also set the renewable share goal to be 40-50% by the year 2040.

Japan initiated its first commercial nuclear power reactor in 1966, establishing nuclear energy as a strategic national priority from 1973 onwards. Following the Fukushima nuclear accident in 2011, this strategy underwent re-evaluation and new plans were introduced to proactively utilize nuclear power.
